headline: Approved Resolution R-26-052 extending the performance period for three FY26 Homeland Security Police Grant Program grants.
summary: Public hearings were held on Ordinance O-26-017, which removes language for a solid waste equipment reserve fund and discontinues the fund, and on Resolution R-26-048, a supplemental appropriation of $1,607,694.55. No one testified at either hearing. Resolution R-26-052 was declared duly adopted after a 14-0 roll call vote.
decisions: Approved Resolution R-26-052, extending the period of performance for three New Hampshire Department of Safety FY26 Homeland Security Police Grant Program grants, by a 14-0 roll call vote.

Ledge Street 
School Community 
Playground Project 
Established: September, 2022 
Enhancing safety, accessibility, and cognitive learning
Current Playground 
The current playground is outdated, small, and does not meet our 
students' needs. It lacks handicap accessibility, age-appropriate 
equipment, and is dangerously close to the road, with hanging wires 
and insufficient green space.
Our Vision  
Encouraging children to engage in collaborative, safe, 
and enjoyable play is vital for nurturing their cognitive 
and social-emotional development. 
Our Plan 
• Utilize the old ball field behind the school to build a 
new playground.  
• The “old” playground will remain in use as long as 
the equipment is safe to utilize. This will also 
increase the number of students outside for 
recess/activities, alleviating several scheduling 
issues.
Challenges: 
• It has been the school district’s stance that school PTOs are responsible for playground erection and 
maintenance. (Plant Operations will assist with minor maintenance, generally under $300.)  
• Low participation in the PTO directly affects its ability to raise funds. This is evident when comparing PTO 
funds to those of other schools in the district. Ledge Street has worked tirelessly over the years to improve 
collaboration.
